correctness.rationale: For every character \(\lambda\) of order \(L\ge3\), induction to the generalized dihedral semidirect product gives a degree-two irreducible whose character is \(\lambda+\lambda^{-1}\) on the abelian kernel and zero on the other coset. Fourier inversion yields the convolution kernel \(2\chi_\lambda\). Exact endpoint convolution norms are the normalized absolute kernel mass. Surjectivity of \(\lambda\) onto the \(L\)-th roots with equal fibers reduces the mass to a complete cyclic cosine average. Dirichlet-kernel identities evaluate that average in the three residue classes, and monotonicity proves that \(L=4\) is the only norm-one value. The finite verifier checks noncyclic product groups but is not used as the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Greenleaf proves that every norm-one idempotent measure on a locally compact group is a character-weighted Haar measure on a compact subgroup. This can recover the qualitative contractive structure after the generalized-dihedral projector kernel is known. It does not provide the exact endpoint norm away from one, the dependence only on \(L=\operatorname{ord}(\lambda)\), the three closed residue-class formulas, or their asymptotics. General compact-group multiplier and abelian minimum-projection results likewise do not supply those quantitative statements.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Standard character/idempotent formulas identify the projector kernel, while Greenleaf classifies the special case in which an idempotent measure already has norm one. Together these facts can explain the qualitative contractive case, but they do not evaluate the projector norm for arbitrary character order. The final theorem additionally proves the exact \(C_L\) formula for every \(L\ge3\), the cyclic quotient reduction, the three residue classes, and the finite-size asymptotics; those quantitative statements are not implied by the inspected prior results.

originality.rationale: The final theorem was compared by implication with compact-group multiplier theory, compact-abelian projection theory, dihedral group-algebra idempotent literature, and Greenleaf’s general norm-one idempotent-measure theorem. Greenleaf broadly covers the qualitative structure of norm-one convolution idempotents, so that aspect is not treated as an independent general novelty claim. None of the inspected sources supplies the exact \(C_L\) formula for every inducing-character order, the generalized-dihedral quotient principle, and the residue-class quantitative behavior together.
residual_risks: The 2024 Dai--Li article is a highly relevant complex-idempotent source whose body was not exposed through the accessed interface; an endpoint-norm observation inside it cannot be ruled out from the material read.

An equivalent formula may occur in older literature under primitive central idempotent, projection constant, or Lebesgue constant terminology without using generalized-dihedral Fourier-projection language.

Classical norm-one idempotent-measure theory already controls the qualitative contractive subcase; the originality assessment therefore rests on the exact quantitative norm family and quotient reduction, not on a new general norm-one idempotent classification.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies the sharp endpoint stability of every nonlinear irreducible spectral block across the entire finite generalized-dihedral family by one intrinsic invariant, character order. It identifies the unique contractive order, gives a group-exponent existence criterion, and exhibits an exact quotient bridge from a noncommutative isotype to a two-frequency cyclic projection. This is a structural family theorem rather than a fixed-size calculation.
